Millenarianism: Belief in a coming fundamental transformation of society.
Trained as a barrister at London's Lincoln's Inn, this statesman led the All-India Muslim League and became the founding governor-general of a new nation in 1947 — who was he?
Muhammad Ali Jinnah: Founder and 1st Governor-General of Pakistan (1876–1948)
Sparked by a 1967 uprising in a West Bengal village, this decades-long rural rebellion against the Indian government has been waged by communist guerrilla groups since — what is it called?
Naxalite–Maoist insurgency: Indian anti-government conflict since 1967.

Sparked by a 1962 coup that toppled a newly crowned king and proclaimed a republic — and even abolished slavery — this conflict pitted royalists backed near the Saudi border against the new government. Which war was it?
North Yemen civil war: 1962–1970 conflict. The war began with a coup d'état carried out in 1962 by revolutionary republicans led by the army under the command of Abdullah al-Sallal.

Banished to a remote province after his wife's affair with Nero, this Roman noble later murdered his ally Galba to seize the throne, becoming the second ruler of the Year of the Four Emperors — who was he?
First featured in a late-12th-century tale by Chrétien de Troyes, this Knight of the Round Table was the original hero of the Grail quest before later authors replaced him with Galahad — who is he?
Perceval: One of King Arthur's legendary Knights.
Known as the 'earth shaker' in Bronze Age cult, this Greek god of the sea and horses could strike his trident to create springs — who is he?
Poseidon: Ancient Greek god of the sea, earthquakes, and horses.
A chartered accountant turned politician, this Rajya Sabha member spent years as an outspoken Aam Aadmi Party figure before defecting to the BJP in April 2026 — who is he?
Born in 1994, this German politician led the Green Youth, then served as her party's women's-policy spokeswoman before becoming co-leader of the Greens in 2022 — who is she?
Ricarda Lang: German politician (born 1994). Ricarda Lang (born 17 January 1994) is a German politician of the Alliance 90/The Greens who has been serving as a member of the Bundestag since 2021.
Produced annually by WWE since 1988, this event's signature match sees wrestlers enter the ring one at a time on a timer rather than all at once — what's the event?
Royal Rumble: World Wrestling Entertainment event series.

A tailor's son turned Navy Board official and MP, he is remembered far less for his politics than for the candid private diary he kept for nearly a decade — a prime window into the Stuart Restoration. Who was he?
Samuel Pepys: English writer and politician (1633–1703)

Once Adolf Hitler's personal chauffeur and bodyguard, this German officer rose to become the highest-ranking commissioned commander in the Waffen-SS despite having no formal staff training — who is he?
Sepp Dietrich: German Nazi politician and SS commander (1892–1966)

Lasting 872 days and killing an estimated 1.5 million from a prewar population of 3.2 million, this WWII blockade of the Soviet Union's second-largest city was never successfully captured — what was it?
Siege of Leningrad: Blockade by the Axis powers, 1941–1944.
Wounded at Gallipoli before entering politics, this businessman led the Nationalist Party as the eighth prime minister of Australia from 1923 to 1929 — who was he?
Stanley Bruce: Prime Minister of Australia from 1923 to 1929. In office, Bruce pursued an energetic and diverse agenda.

Running from 1912 to 1926 and named for its reigning emperor, this period in Japanese history saw political power shift from a group of elder statesmen to the country's parliamentary parties — what do historians call it?
Taishō era: Period of Japanese history from 1912 to 1926.
A Whig historian famed for his prose, he both wrote a seminal "History of England" and played a major role in shaping India's education policy — who was he?
Thomas Babington Macaulay: British historian and politician (1800–1859)
This Mitsubishi engineer had the extraordinarily unlucky distinction of being caught in both the Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings in August 1945 — and lived to tell about it. Who is he?
Tsutomu Yamaguchi: Japanese atomic bombing survivor.

This King of Italy also claimed the titles Emperor of Ethiopia and King of the Albanians after Italy's invasions of those countries, and reigned through the entire rise and fall of the Fascist regime — who was he?
Victor Emmanuel III: King of Italy from 1900 to 1946.

Launched as Operation Enduring Freedom in response to the 9/11 attacks, this two-decade conflict began by toppling the Taliban-ruled Islamic Emirate with help from the Northern Alliance — what was it?
War in Afghanistan (2001–2021): U.S Armed conflict in South Asia.
A descendant of the Viking Rollo and once called 'the Bastard,' this Duke of Normandy won the Battle of Hastings in 1066 and became the first Norman king of England — who was he?
William the Conqueror: King of England from 1066 to 1087.

A former prosecutor general, he served the shortest term of any elected leader in his country's democratic history before removal in 2025 — and is now serving life for leading an insurrection. Which South Korean president is it?
Yoon Suk Yeol: President of South Korea from 2022 to 2025.
Which one below was born first?
John Ray (born 1627) is the earliest of the four. John Ray (29 November 1627 – 17 January 1705) was an English Christian naturalist and one of the earliest English parson-naturalists.
Which of these four is the eldest?

Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four. Omar Khayyam (1048–1131) was a Persian poet and polymath, known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, and Persian literature.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four. The c. 215 treatises that survive today mainly deal with alchemy and chemistry, magic, and Shi'ite religious philosophy.
Which of these four has been around longest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these four was released earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Edwin McMillan is a physicist. McMillan co-invented the synchrotron with Vladimir Veksler, and after the war he returned to the Berkeley Radiation Laboratory to build them.
Who among these is a chemist?
Henry Taube is a chemist. Taube completed his undergraduate and master's degrees at the University of Saskatchewan, and his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley.
What is the atomic number of Sodium?
Sodium: Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
In what year was Viktor Yushchenko born?
Viktor Yushchenko: Yushchenko's first career was in the banking industry.
In what year was Giordano Bruno born?
Giordano Bruno: Bruno's pantheism was not taken lightly by the church, nor was his teaching of metempsychosis regarding the reincarnation of the soul.
In what year was Tomitaro Makino born?
Tomitaro Makino: Tomitaro Makino (牧野 富太郎, Makino Tomitarō; 24 April 1862 – 18 January 1957) was a pioneer Japanese botanist noted for his taxonomic work.
In what year did Paul Allen die?
Paul Allen: Paul Gardner Allen (January 21, 1953 – October 15, 2018) was an American businessman, computer programmer, and investor.
In what year did Mikhail Lomonosov die?
Mikhail Lomonosov: One of the founders of modern geology, Lomonosov was also a poet and influenced the formation of the modern Russian literary language.
In what year was Scurvy discovered?
Scurvy: Scurvy or scorbutus is a deficiency disease (state of malnutrition) resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
In what year was Polonium discovered?
Polonium: Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84.
Spironolactone: Pfizer. Spironolactone, sold under the brand name Aldactone among others, is classed as a diuretic medication.
In which country is Gaboon viper?
Gaboon viper: Gabon. It is the largest member of the genus Bitis.
Who is credited with discovering Radon?
Radon: Friedrich Ernst Dorn. Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Who is credited with discovering Tautavel Man?
Tautavel Man: Henry de Lumley. Tautavel Man refers to the archaic humans which—from approximately 550,000 to 400,000 years ago—inhabited the Caune de l’Arago, a limestone cave in Tautavel, France.
Who is credited with discovering MDMA?
MDMA: Anton Köllisch. MDMA was first synthesized in 1912 by Merck chemist Anton Köllisch.
In this science fiction comedy-drama, a man undergoes a procedure to shrink his body and start a new life in a miniature experimental community. What film is it?
Adansonia is a genus of medium-to-large deciduous trees known as baobabs or boababs.

With roughly 370 million individuals, this migratory thrush outnumbers red-winged blackbirds and starlings across its home continent, despite being misnamed after an unrelated European species — what is it?
American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.
Largely self-taught, this Dutch tradesman-turned-scientist pioneered the use of the microscope and is commonly called the 'Father of Microbiology' — who is he?
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (AHN-tə-nee vahn LAY-vən-hook, -huuk; 24 October 1632 - 26 August 1723) was a Dutch microbiologist and microscopist in the Golden Age of Dutch art, science and technology.
Caused by poor circulation, lost nerve supply, or simple disuse, this process shrinks a cell, organ, or tissue below its normal mature size — what's it called?
Atrophy is the partial or complete wasting away of a part of the body.
Native to Southeast Asia, the glossy heart-shaped leaves of this evergreen vine are chewed together with areca nut — name the plant?
Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.

Developed in Germany from the Old English Bulldog and the now-extinct Bullenbeisser, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog breed is known for its square muzzle, underbite, and powerful bite — name the breed?
Boxer (dog breed) is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.

One species in this genus of flowering shrubs, native to southern China and Indochina, has its leaves processed into the world's tea, while thousands of ornamental cultivars exist for the garden. Name the genus?
Camellia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Theaceae.
A secondarily aquatic clade within the order that also includes hippos, this infraorder covers whales, dolphins and porpoises, along with extinct relatives like Basilosaurus — which group of animals?

Cetacean are marine mammals belonging to the infraorder Cetacea, a secondarily aquatic clade under the order Artiodactyla that include whales, dolphins, porpoises and extinct groups such as Basilosaurus.
This tangor — a mandarin-orange cross — typically splits into seven to fourteen easy-to-peel segments — which fruit?
Clementine (Citrus clementina) is a tangor, a citrus fruit hybrid between a willowleaf mandarin orange (C. deliciosa) and a sweet orange (C. sinensis).
Made up of subregions called the genu, rostrum, trunk, and splenium, this thick nerve tract lets the brain's two hemispheres communicate — what is it?
Corpus callosum (Latin for "tough body"), also callosal commissure, is a wide, thick nerve tract, consisting of a flat bundle of commissural fibers, beneath the cerebral cortex in the brain.

Known by names ranging from the clinical to the crude to the childish — 'number two', 'dropping a deuce', 'doo-doo' — this basic biological process expels solid waste from the digestive tract. Name the process?

Defecation (or defaecation) follows digestion and is the necessary biological process by which organisms eliminate a solid, semisolid, or liquid waste material known as feces (or faeces) from the digestive tract via the anus or cloaca.
Best known for a single spiky, strong-smelling fruit beloved across Southeast Asia, this plant genus also includes eight other species with edible fruit — which genus?
Durio is a genus of plants in the family Malvaceae.
This inflammation of the small intestine is most often caused by contaminated food or drink, though NSAIDs, radiation, and autoimmune conditions can also trigger it. What is it?
Enteritis is inflammation of the small intestine. Duodenitis, jejunitis, and ileitis are subtypes of enteritis which are localised to a specific part of the small intestine.
Colloquially called 'squirting,' this phenomenon involves fluid from the Skene's gland and is physiologically distinct from coital incontinence — what is it?
Female ejaculation is characterized as an expulsion of fluid from the Skene's gland at the lower end of the urethra during or before an orgasm.
Often bonded to glucose to form table sugar, this white, water-soluble simple sugar occurs naturally in honey, tree and vine fruits, and most root vegetables — name this sugar?
Fructose is a common monosaccharide, i.e.

Designed at a major tech company in 2007 by Robert Griesemer, Rob Pike, and Ken Thompson, this statically typed, compiled programming language borrows C-like syntax while adding garbage collection and built-in concurrency support — name the language?
Go (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose programming language that is statically typed and compiled.
Hailed by Time as a 2019 'Pioneer' yet condemned as a mad scientist, which Chinese biophysicist announced in 2018 that he'd created the first gene-edited human babies?
He Jiankui (pinyin: H Jinku HUH KWAY; born 1984) is a Chinese biophysicist known for his controversial first use of genome editing in humans in 2018.
One of the six Celtic nations, this peninsula in northwest France was known as Armorica under Roman rule before becoming an independent kingdom and later a duchy. What region is it?
Hydra (genus) is a genus of small freshwater hydrozoans in the phylum Cnidaria.
An ISO standard defines it as "a new or changed entity, realizing or redistributing value" — and it's related to, but not the same as, invention. What word are we after?
Innovation is the practical implementation of ideas that result in the creation or improvements of goods or services.

Called 'the greatest investor on Wall Street,' this founder of Renaissance Technologies made his fortune using mathematical models, after co-developing a key concept in differential geometry — who is he?
Jim Simons (April 25, 1938 - May 10, 2024) was an American hedge fund manager, investor, mathematician, and philanthropist.

Coined by naturalist Christopher Merret in 1667 to describe a forked-tailed bird of prey, this name was originally applied to the buzzard before settling permanently on its red-plumed cousin — what's the name?
Kite (bird) is the common name for certain birds of prey in the family Accipitridae, particularly in the subfamilies Elaninae and Perninae and certain genera within Buteoninae and Harpaginae.
Used to treat an underactive thyroid and even a severe form called myxedema coma, this synthetic version of thyroxine (T4) takes about six weeks to reach a steady blood level — what's this drug?
Levothyroxine is a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4). It is used to treat thyroid hormone deficiency (hypothyroidism), including a severe form known as myxedema coma.
The sole species in its genus, this South Chinese fruit has a sweet, mildly tart flavor and a distinctive rose-like floral aroma — name it?
Lychee (US also) are the fruit of the tree Litchi chinensis, the sole member of the genus Litchi, part of the soapberry family, Sapindaceae.

Encompassing complex, functional, and measure theory as major subfields, this branch of mathematics studies real numbers, sequences, series, and limits with rigor formalized in the 19th century — which field?
Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
Carrying NATO's 'Hind' codename and its crews' affectionate 'flying tank,' this Soviet machine is both an attack craft and a low-capacity troop carrier. What is it?
Mil Mi-24 (NATO reporting name: Hind) is a large helicopter gunship, attack helicopter and low-capacity troop transport with room for eight passengers.
When the radial fibres of the iris over-dilate the pupil beyond its normal light response, what do doctors call this condition?
Mydriasis is the dilation of the pupil, usually having a non-physiological cause, or sometimes a physiological pupillary response.
Sold in packs needing a desiccant to keep it from absorbing moisture, this seaweed sheet was once used as currency and shrine offerings in Japan — what is it?
Nori is a dried edible seaweed used in Japanese cuisine, usually made from species of the red algae genus Pyropia, including P. yezoensis and P. tenera.
Often linked to polycystic ovary syndrome or pelvic inflammatory disease, this fluid-filled sac can cause severe pain if it ruptures or twists — what is it?
Ovarian cyst is a fluid-filled sac within the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.
Built for the sea, it sports a spiny tongue and powerful jaws to grip slippery fish, then swallows them whole mid-swim. Which animal splits its life half on land, half in the water?
Penguin are a group of flightless semi-aquatic sea birds which live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere.
The sole genus in its plant subfamily, this evergreen conifer bears needle-like leaves in bunches of two to five and carries its seeds on woody cones — name the tree?
Pine is any conifer in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae.

Caused by the loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15, this rare genetic disorder leads to weak muscles and poor feeding in infancy, then constant hunger and risk of obesity in childhood — what's it called?

Prader–Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by a loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15. A similar mechanism occurs in Angelman syndrome, except the defective chromosome 15 is from the mother, or two copies are from the father.
The sole member of the genus Setonix, this cat-sized, mainly nocturnal Australian marsupial famously inhabits Rottnest Island — what is it?
Quokka (Setonix brachyurus) is a small macropod about the size of a domestic cat.
First created near Darmstadt in 1994 and named for the physicist who discovered X-rays, this extremely radioactive element exists as only a handful of atoms with no practical use — which one is it?
Roentgenium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
Which genus of large, tropical, many-legged predators takes its name from ancient Greek words meaning roughly 'thorn' and 'earthworm'?
Scolopendra (from Ancient Greek (sklops), meaning "thorn", and (nteron), meaning "earthworm") is a species-rich genus of large tropical centipedes of the family Scolopendridae.
About 0.01% of people are born with this condition, in which the heart typically ends up on the right side of the chest instead of the left — what is it?
Situs inversus is a congenital condition in which the major visceral organs are reversed or mirrored from their normal positions.

Held together by its own gravity, this luminous sphere of plasma is the type of object our Sun is, with roughly 4,000 of them visible to the naked eye on a clear night - what are these objects called?
Star is a luminous spheroid of plasma held together by self-gravity.
Deriving its name from a French word for crushed oak bark used in hide-curing, this class of astringent plant compounds binds to and precipitates proteins and other organic molecules — what is it?
Tannin (or tannoids) are a class of astringent, polyphenolic biomolecules that bind to and precipitate proteins and various other organic compounds including amino acids and alkaloids.
Shaped like a butterfly and located in the neck just below the Adam's apple, this endocrine gland's two lobes are joined by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus — name the gland?
Thyroid is an endocrine gland in vertebrates. The lower two thirds of the lobes are connected by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus (pl.: isthmi).
Named from the Greek word for 'cheese' after being first isolated from milk protein in 1846, this standard amino acid is more water-loving than its close relative phenylalanine. Name the amino acid?
Tyrosine (symbol Tyr or Y) or 4-hydroxyphenylalanine is one of the 20 standard amino acids that are used by cells to synthesize proteins.

In physics, this phenomenon occurs when two coherent waves combine according to their phase difference, producing either a boosted 'constructive' amplitude or a canceling 'destructive' one — what's the effect called?
Wave interference is a phenomenon in which two coherent waves are combined by adding their intensities or displacements with due consideration for their phase difference.

Released from prison in June 2025 to resume leading Turkey's nationalist Victory Party, this politician previously served as deputy leader of the far-right Nationalist Movement Party in the mid-2010s — who is he?
Ümit Özdağ (born 3 March 1961) is a Turkish politician who returned to his position as the current leader of the Victory Party after being released from prison on 17 June 2025.
Nicknamed for the stripes on its legs and body, this day-biting mosquito native to Southeast Asia spreads dengue, yellow fever, and Chikungunya — what is it called?
Aedes albopictus: Species of mosquito. The insect is called a tiger mosquito as it has stripes, as does a tiger.
This diverse group of photosynthetic organisms ranges from microscopic plankton to seaweeds 50 metres long — yet excludes the land plants entirely. What is it?
Algae: Diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. Algae (AL-jee, UK also AL-ghee; sing.: alga) are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms.
Critically endangered with barely two dozen wild individuals estimated in 2007, this big cat subspecies survives along the Russian-Chinese border in the Primorye region — which spotted predator?
Amur leopard: Subspecies of large cat. The Amur leopard (Panthera pardus orientalis) is a leopard subspecies native to the Primorye region of southeastern Russia and northern China.

A political economy professor turned finance minister after a 1926 coup, this Portuguese dictator ruled his corporatist 'New State' from 1932 until 1968, in one of modern Europe's longest authoritarian regimes — who is he?
António de Oliveira Salazar: Prime Minister of Portugal from 1932 to 1968.
Most commonly caused by liver cirrhosis and its resulting high blood pressure in the portal system, this condition is the abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity — which one?
Ascites: Abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen.

A North American bird of prey and sea eagle, found near large open water and old-growth forest. Its range spans most of Canada, Alaska, the contiguous U.S., and northern Mexico. This is the national bird of the United States. What is it?
Bald eagle: Bird of prey species of North America.
Native to Southeast Asia, the heart-shaped leaves of this pepper-family vine are chewed with areca nut, despite links to serious health risks — which plant?
Betel: Species of plant. Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.
Launched as the 7X7 program in 1978 and designed to complement the larger 747, which American wide-body airliner first entered service with United Airlines in 1982?
Too small to fuse hydrogen but massive enough to briefly burn deuterium, these objects between 13 and 80 Jupiter masses cool over time through spectral classes M, L, T, and Y — what are they called?
With more than 220 species and over 26,000 registered cultivars, this flowering plant genus includes the very species whose leaves are processed into tea worldwide — which genus?
Camellia: Genus of flowering plants in the tea family.
A woody shrub native to South America, this starchy tuber yields tapioca and, when grated and toasted, becomes Brazil's farofa and West Africa's garri — what crop is it?
Cassava: Staple crop. Although a perennial plant, cassava is extensively cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions as an annual crop for its edible starchy tuberous root.
Known by the common name 'greater celandine,' this perennial flowering plant belongs to the poppy family and is native to Europe and western Asia — what's its scientific name?
Chelidonium majus: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family. One of two species in the genus Chelidonium, it is native to Europe and western Asia and introduced widely in North America.
Dubbed the 'father of information theory,' this polymath was the first to apply Boolean algebra to digital circuits and helped found the field of artificial intelligence — who is he?

A summer migrant to Europe and Asia that winters in Africa, this bird tricks other species into raising its young by laying eggs that mimic the host's, and even disguises itself as a hawk — what bird is it?
Common cuckoo: Species of bird. It is a brood parasite, which means it lays eggs in the nests of other bird species, particularly of dunnocks, meadow pipits, and reed warblers.

This blood-feeding parasitic insect, scientifically Pthirus pubis, typically lives in coarse body hair and diverged from a gorilla-infecting relative about 3.3 million years ago — what is it commonly called?
Crab louse: Species of insect. The crab louse or pubic louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.
This Swedish tech entrepreneur founded and chairs a streaming giant, with a net worth estimated at $8.7 billion in December 2025 — who is he?
This bodily process breaks large food molecules into water-soluble components through both mechanical action like chewing and chemical action from enzymes — what's it called?
Digestion: Biological process of breaking down food.
Sometimes nicknamed 'math dyslexia' even though it's a distinct condition, this learning disorder involves persistent difficulty understanding numbers and performing calculations — what is it called?
This stage of development begins right after fertilization, progressing from a single-celled zygote through a ball of cells called a morula — what is it called?
Embryo: Multicellular diploid eukaryote in its earliest stage of development.
This white solid is prized for binding iron and calcium ions into water-soluble complexes — handy for dissolving scale — and goes by a four-letter acronym. What is it?
This principle describes how a changing magnetic field generates an electric current, underpinning the operation of transformers, generators, and motors — what is it called?
Faraday's law of induction: Basic law of electromagnetism.
Originally focused on water, this branch of physics studies liquids, gases, and plasmas, with applications from geophysics to aerospace engineering — which field?
Fluid mechanics: Branch of physics. Fluid mechanics is the branch of physics concerned with the mechanics of fluids (liquids, gases, and plasmas) and the forces on them.
Bound together by gravity, this vast system of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter can range from a dwarf with under a thousand stars to a supergiant with a hundred trillion — what is it?
Galaxy: System of stars and interstellar matter. The word is derived from the Greek galaxias (γαλαξίας), meaning 'milky', a reference to the Milky Way galaxy that contains the Solar System.
Caused by a genetic variant in the UGT1A1 gene, this harmless liver condition slows the breakdown of bilirubin and can trigger jaundice during stress, exercise, or fasting — what is it called?
Gilbert's syndrome: Medical condition. It is typically inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern and occasionally in an autosomal dominant pattern depending on the type of variant.
An Augustinian friar and abbot in Brno, this Austrian biologist spent 1856 to 1863 crossbreeding pea plants — work that earned him posthumous fame as the founder of genetics. Who was he?
Gregor Mendel: Austrian biologist and friar (1822–1884)

This English physician co-wrote the first English-language medical textbook on homosexuality in 1897, coined the term 'narcissism,' and penned an early public account of a mescaline trip he took on himself. Who was he?
Havelock Ellis: British physician, eugenicist, writer, and social reformer (1859–1939)
Hardy enough to survive winters as cold as -43°C, this shrub genus's aggressive roots fight soil erosion, and its berries and leaves are turned into food and skincare products — which genus?
Hippophae: Genus of flowering plants including sea buckthorn.
This Greek-derived name means 'thin skin' and refers to a piece of mucosal tissue that partially covers the vaginal opening in many mammals — which structure?
Hymen: Membrane that surrounds or partially covers the vaginal opening.
Symbolized by the '∞' sign and debated by philosophers since ancient Greece, this endless concept was later shown by Georg Cantor to come in different sizes when applied to sets. What is it?
Infinity: Mathematical concept. Infinity is something which is boundless, limitless, or endless.
This neo-Keynesian economist gave his name to a model for censored data — the 'tobit' — while advising the Fed and championing government action against recessions; who is he?
James Tobin: American economist and Nobel Laureate (1918–2002)
While tinkering with electromagnets, this American physicist discovered self-inductance and went on to become the very first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution — who was he?
Joseph Henry: American physicist and inventor (1797–1878)
Made from shredded pastry dough layered with cheese and soaked in sugar syrup, this Arab dessert is especially popular during Ramadan, with a famous variant hailing from Nablus — what is it?
Formulated in 1834, this principle of electromagnetism states that an induced current always flows in a direction that opposes the very change in magnetic field that created it — which principle?
Lenz's law: Electromagnetic opposition to change.

Providing the USAF with intercontinental strategic airlift for oversized cargo, this jumbo transport is among the largest military aircraft ever built and shares lineage with the smaller Starlifter — what is it?
Lockheed C-5 Galaxy: American heavy military transport aircraft.
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, and the quokka among its 63 recognized species — what is it?
Macropodidae: Family of marsupial mammals. Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.
A Zainichi Korean entrepreneur, this founder and CEO of SoftBank turned a $20 million bet on Alibaba in 2000 into a stake worth around $75 billion — who is he?
Developed in 1955 and later sold under the brand name Dianabol, this anabolic steroid was once widely used for physique and performance enhancement — what is it?
Metandienone: Androgen and anabolic steroid. It is also used non-medically for physique- and performance-enhancing purposes.

Prized for their fur and related to weasels and otters, these semiaquatic carnivores have established wild populations in Britain and Denmark after farm escapes and animal-rights releases — what are they?
Mink: Mammal in the family Mustelidae.
This contagious, vaccine-preventable viral disease is best known for causing painful swelling of the glands beside the jaw — its hallmark symptom. What is it?
Mumps: Human disease caused by paramyxovirus.
Commonly called horsehair worms, these parasitoid animals get their nickname from the Gordian knot because of how they tangle themselves up — what phylum is this?

Nematomorpha: Phylum of parasitoid animals; horsehair worms. The adult worms are free-living, but the larvae are parasitic on arthropods, such as beetles, cockroaches, mantises, orthopterans, and crustaceans.

Introduced in 2001 and originally developed under the name Tier II+, which remotely piloted, high-altitude surveillance aircraft supports the US Air Force with long-endurance radar and infrared sensors?
Northrop Grumman RQ-4 Global Hawk: Unmanned surveillance aircraft. It was initially designed by Ryan Aeronautical (now part of Northrop Grumman), and known as Tier II+ during development.

Traditionally eaten whole in French cuisine, with diners often covering their heads with a napkin while doing so, this small Eurasian songbird's population crashed from overhunting despite EU protection — which bird?
Ortolan bunting: Species of bird in Eurasia.
Strong curved beak, upright stance, clawed feet — this order of roughly 410 tropical bird species, including the cockatoos, faces a higher extinction risk than any comparable bird group — what is it?
Parrot: Order of birds. One-third of all parrot species are threatened by extinction, with a higher aggregate extinction risk (IUCN Red List Index) than any other comparable bird group.

Caused by a lack of intrinsic factor — often from an autoimmune attack on the stomach — this vitamin B12 deficiency disorder brings gradual fatigue, a smooth red tongue, and numbness in the hands and feet — which condition?
Pernicious anemia: Lack of red blood cells due to vitamin B12 deficiency.
